brief: Cash flows have risen faster than capex, pushing US corporate financing surpluses toward historic highs outside crisis periods: the Q2 2026 all-corporate surplus reached about 2% of GDP, near highs since 1952, and the non-financial surplus about 1.5% of GDP, the highest since 1958. JPM attributes contained aggregate capex growth partly to AI capex crowding out other capex, keeping capex-to-GDP well below the 1990s tech-bubble pace. These surpluses cut corporate funding needs and sustain buybacks, especially outside tech; global buybacks are tracking $1.7tr this year, $1.3tr from US companies, though JPM expects tech's rising buyback share to reverse over the next 5-10 years as AI infrastructure spending erodes hyperscaler surpluses. Separately, on momentum-based positioning: bond-future shorts extended again after today's sell-off (10y UST -1.7, Bund -1.5, OAT-vs-Bund -2.5, energy futures still extreme long), while equity, gold and bitcoin signals stayed off extremes. On bitcoin, spot price moved above JPM's implied roughly $85k production cost after 280 days below it, versus 224 days in the 2018 down-cycle, a shift JPM reads as reducing forced miner selling, alongside a structural pivot of miners toward AI that cut network hashrate and difficulty about 19% and 15% from October's peak.
